title: Section equation for the stabilizer component
statement: Under the hypotheses of single stabilizer descent [lem-sbc-affine-torsor-split-label-laws], set F to the intersection of the K-equalizer subalgebras, U=D(algebraMap H F (ι g)), and q:D(algebraMap H C (ι g))->U to the restricted inclusion spectrum map. There exists a map s:U->Y over Spec R whose pullback along q is the selected x-th split section. In particular s followed by p is U->Spec H->Spec R. No openness assertion is included, and neither F nor the descended map is arbitrary.

source.place: Tag 03SF, finite Galois covers and permutation sets; stabilizer quotient argument

proof.text: D(h_C) is nonempty and irreducible: the zero prime supplies a point since h_C is nonzero, and the puncture is open in the spectrum of a domain. A morphism into a split finite cover over T from this connected source has clopen inverse images of its summands; the summand containing the zero prime contains the entire image. Lifting through that open summand and projecting to T shows it is exactly the split section with the evaluated label. This is proved locally, reproducing the reconstruction argument whose original declaration in SplitAction is private.

For each zeta in K, the stabilizer equation hK identifies the evaluated label of deck(zeta) followed by the selected split section with x. Apply reconstruction to conclude that this composite is the selected section. The finite map j to the affine D(g) makes Y affine (Mathlib IsAffineOpen.Spec_basicOpen and isAffine_of_isAffineHom).

Apply affine invariant basic-open descent to the selected section and the established invariance, obtaining s with q followed by s equal to that section. The restriction identity Hom.resLE_comp_ι and composition of Spec maps give q followed by the natural U-to-Spec-R map b equal to k followed by t. Deck maps fix k followed by t by fixedPunctureDeck_base and hk. Apply uniqueness of affine invariant basic-open descent to this structural map: both s followed by p (using fixedSplitSection_base) and b pull back to k followed by t, hence they agree. Package s and its two equations. No Galois classification theorem, localization-invariants axiom or new sorry is used.

proof_origin.note: The complete Lean proof establishes label reconstruction, invariance and the base equation; the affine invariant-ring calculation is proved in a new generic module, without Galois-cover classification.

lean.statement:
theorem affine_torsor_single_stabilizer_component_section
    (R H : CommRingCat.{u}) (g : R) (ι : R →+* H)
    (C : Type u) [CommRing C] [Algebra H C] [IsDomain C]
    [Module.Finite H C] [Module.FaithfullyFlat H C]
    (G : Type u) [Group G] [Finite G]
    (ρ : G → C →ₐ[H] C)
    (hρone : ρ 1 = AlgHom.id H C)
    (hρmul : ∀ a b, ρ (a * b) = (ρ a).comp (ρ b))
    (hne : algebraMap H C (ι g) ≠ 0)
    {Y : Scheme.{u}} (p : Y ⟶ Spec R)
    (j : Y ⟶ Scheme.Opens.toScheme (X := Spec R) (PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen g))
    (hj : j ≫ Scheme.Opens.ι (X := Spec R) (PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen g) = p)
    [IsFinite j] [Etale j]
    (hEt : Etale (Scheme.Opens.ι (X := Spec (CommRingCat.of C))
      (PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen (algebraMap H C (ι g))) ≫
      Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap H C))))
    (hrot : ∀ (Ω : Type u) [Field Ω] (a b : C →+* Ω),
      a.comp (algebraMap H C) = b.comp (algebraMap H C) →
      a (algebraMap H C (ι g)) ≠ 0 →
      ∃! ζ : G, a.comp (ρ ζ).toRingHom = b)
    (d : ℕ)
    (T : Scheme.{u}) (t : T ⟶ Spec R)
    (k : Scheme.Opens.toScheme (X := Spec (CommRingCat.of C))
      (PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen (algebraMap H C (ι g))) ⟶ T)
    (hk : k ≫ t = Scheme.Opens.ι (X := Spec (CommRingCat.of C))
      (PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen (algebraMap H C (ι g))) ≫
      Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap H C)) ≫
      Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom ι))
    (δ : pullback p t ≅ ∐ fun _ : Fin d ↦ T)
    (hδ : δ.hom ≫ Sigma.desc (fun _ : Fin d ↦ 𝟙 T) = pullback.snd p t)
    (x : Fin d) (K : Subgroup G)
    (hK : ∀ ζ, ζ ∈ K ↔
      fixedPunctureDescentAction R H g ι C G ρ hρone hρmul hne
        p T t k hk d δ hδ ζ x = x) :
    let F := (⨅ ζ : K, AlgHom.equalizer (ρ ζ.val) (AlgHom.id H C) : Subalgebra H C)
    let U : (Spec (CommRingCat.of F)).Opens := PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen (algebraMap H F (ι g))
    let q := (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom F.val.toRingHom)).resLE
      U (PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen (algebraMap H C (ι g))) (by
        change PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen (algebraMap H C (ι g)) ≤
          PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen (algebraMap H C (ι g))
        rfl)
    ∃ s : Scheme.Opens.toScheme (X := Spec (CommRingCat.of F)) U ⟶ Y,
      s ≫ p = (Scheme.Opens.ι (X := Spec (CommRingCat.of F)) U ≫
        Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap H F))) ≫
          Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom ι) ∧
      q ≫ s = fixedSplitSection p t k d δ x

statement_change.old_statement: The quotient restriction followed by a chosen open stabilizer component recovers the chosen split section.
statement_change.what: The old Lean statement quantifies over arbitrary F and f, with no openness or projection hypotheses, and is false for the trivial torsor over Q and a two-point split cover. Replace it with existence of a map descending the selected section, without openness. The original parent statement stays identical.
